Manx: 10 May 99
Dear Mr Wood,

I beg leave to thank you for your kind offer of the first edition of Kelly’s Manx Grammar, but as I already have a copy of it, it would not be right for me to accept it. This does not make the slightest difference in my estimation of your kindness. There is one favour I should like to ask you, but if you do not see your way to grant it, please do not take any notice of it. I should like to see “Leo’s Manx Grammar” — either the German copy, or your translation of it — only for my own satisfaction. I am merely a collector and preserver of the spoken language, and have taken down thousands of colloquial expressions which would otherwise have been lost.
I have at least five hundred proverbs  in addition to those you collected.

There is a gentleman of Peel of the name of Goodwin, who is taking up the grammatical structure of the language, and he is fully qualified to do so, as he understands Gaelic (Scotch) and Erse (Irish) as well as Manx. He is taking as his basis “O’ Growney’s Lessons in Irish”, and I am really surprised at the similarity between Manx and Irish. In fact the syntax of the Irish language can be easily adapted to Mann. His book will soon be published.
With kindest regards to you and Mrs Wood and again thanking you for your very kind offer.
English: I am very appreciative of your beautiful Christmas gift, and I am obliged to you for it.

Manx: I am
English: I send body and health to you and your wife.

Manx: Yours faithfully
Clauge
21 Dec 99
G. W. Wood,
Vainsher Veen,
Ta mee screeu dhyt, dy vod fys ve ayd dy dooar mee y shenn chaslys jeh Ellan Vannin ooilley cairagh.
English: I am writing to you so you may know that I received the old image of the Isle of Man all as it should be.

Manx: Cha naik mee rieau y lheid roie, as shynney lhiam eh dy mie.
English: I have never seen the like before, and I love it well.

Manx: Ta mee soiaghey mooar jeh dty Nastey-Nollick aalin, as ta mee kianlt booise dhyt er y hon.
English: I am very appreciative of your beautiful Christmas gift, and I am obliged to you for it.

Manx: Ta mee cur corp-as-slaynt dhyt’s as da dty ven heshey.
English: I send body and health to you and your wife.

Manx: Ollick ghennal erriu as Blein Vaynrey Noa tra hig y traa.
English: Merry Christmas to you and a Happy New Year when the time comes.

Manx: Ta shen yeearree my chree erriuish ny neesht.
English: That is my heart’s desire for you both.

Manx: Dhyts dy firrinagh
Juan Clague y Fer lhee
